Introduction | Whakapuakitanga
Reporting group
These climate statements (referred to in this document as the climate-related disclosure) are for IAG New Zealand Limited, a licensed 
insurer in Aotearoa New Zealand, and its subsidiaries (together referred to as IAG New Zealand or ‘we’ or ‘us’). IAG New Zealand Limited 
is the largest general insurer in the country, trading under brands including AMI, State, NZI, NAC, Lumley and Lantern, as well as 
providing the general insurance products distributed by ASB, BNZ, Westpac, The Co-operative Bank and other intermediaries.
IAG New Zealand Limited is a wholly-owned subsidiary of IAG (NZ) Holdings Limited. There are other subsidiaries of IAG (NZ) Holdings 
Limited. These other subsidiaries of IAG (NZ) Holdings Limited are not included in IAG New Zealand’s reporting group. 
Insurance Australia Group Limited (referred to in this document as IAG Group or Group) is the ultimate holding company of IAG New 
Zealand Limited and IAG (NZ) Holdings Limited. Its shares are quoted on the Australian Stock Exchange and it has notes listed on 
the NZX Debt Market operated by NZX Limited. IAG Group has released a voluntary climate-related disclosure for FY25 (IAG Group 
Sustainability Report), which can be found within IAG Group’s FY25 Annual Report on the IAG Group website. 
This climate-related disclosure is prepared for IAG New Zealand. The disclosure also incorporates the New Zealand business of IAG 
Group, to the extent material, as required by the Financial Markets Conduct (Climate-related Disclosures for Foreign Listed Issuers) 
Exemption Notice 2024 (Exemption Notice). IAG Group is exempt from preparing separate climate statements in respect of its New 
Zealand business and investment assets by the Exemption Notice, as set out in its FY25 Annual Report. 
The New Zealand business of IAG Group comprises IAG (NZ) Holdings Limited and its subsidiaries, which include IAG New Zealand 
Limited, as well as First Rescue New Zealand Limited, IAG RepairHub Limited, and Home Hub Limited (together the Hub Services).  
IAG Group has not identified any material disclosures that are required by the Aotearoa New Zealand Climate Standards relating to  
its New Zealand business beyond those relating to IAG New Zealand Limited which are included in this climate-related disclosure.
This year we have refined our view of primary users of this disclosure, to focus on existing and potential investors in IAG Group and 
reinsurers. This is narrower than our view in FY24 which also included customers. As a consequence, the statements made in this 
disclosure reflect information which is material to those primary users. 
Note that although certain IAG Group documents are referenced in this climate-related disclosure – including the IAG Group 
Sustainability Report and the IAG Climate Action Plan – these are not referred to in order for IAG New Zealand to meet its obligations 
under the Aotearoa New Zealand Climate Standards and are not intended to form part of IAG New Zealand’s climate-related disclosure.
Important information
This climate-related disclosure contains forward-looking statements including statements regarding IAG New Zealand’s climate-related 
strategy, targets, goals, ambitions, intent, belief, objectives, commitments and current expectations. Any forward-looking statements 
included in this climate-related disclosure are current only as at the date of this disclosure, 8 August 2025, and may change. Given 
the emerging and uncertain nature of the content, readers are cautioned not to place reliance on forward-looking statements in this 
disclosure. 
This disclosure includes representations relating to climate change, including but not limited to, climate and disaster resilience and 
other sustainability related statements, commitments, goals, targets, projections, scenarios, assessments, forecasts and expectations. 
These statements are not guarantees, predictions or forecasts of future climate-related outcomes, financial performance or share prices. 
There are significant uncertainties, limitations and assumptions in the metrics and modelling on which these statements rely. Such 
statements involve judgements, attitudes, known and unknown risks, uncertainties and assumptions beyond IAG New Zealand’s control, 
and are subject to assumptions, limitations, and contingencies, particularly as to inputs, available data and information which is likely 
to change. Readers are therefore cautioned not to place reliance on such statements.
We base those statements and opinions on reasonable information we know at the date of publication, being 8 August 2025. We do not:

This disclosure should not be relied upon as a recommendation, forecast or guarantee by or expectation of IAG New Zealand, its related 
or controlled entities or officers, directors, employees or agents. The forward-looking statements in this disclosure should be read in 
the context of the variables, risks, uncertainties and other factors outlined in this Important information or mentioned elsewhere in this

Strategy | Rautaki
IAG’s purpose is to make your world a safer place. We help our customers – individuals, households, and businesses – manage risk and 
recover from unexpected events. Weather events, like floods, cyclones, wildfires, and storms, can cause damage and insurance can play 
a role in assisting our customers’ recovery in these situations. 
Responding to the impacts of climate change is important to our business. The frequency and severity of weather-related events may 
impact how we price and underwrite our products and respond to claims. We maintain reinsurance to provide capital support. We also 
work with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to stress test our resilience to severe but plausible risks which includes consideration of the 
risk of physical climate impacts.
1.1	 Material climate-related risks and opportunities

physical risks for IAG New Zealand as at FY25, which are described in Table 1 below. These risks are not listed in order of materiality. We

view of primary users. As a result, we have disclosed the information that is considered material to primary users of this climate-related 
disclosure. In addition, we have reclassified some risks.1 
Table 1 also sets out the anticipated impacts of each material climate-related risk and the climate-related scenarios and time horizons in

1.2	 IAG New Zealand’s business model and strategy
IAG New Zealand is Aotearoa New Zealand’s largest general insurer. Our business model is to provide a range of retail and commercial 
insurance products to individuals, households and businesses. These products include vehicle, property, contents, business 
interruption, and liability insurance. The products are sold either directly under IAG New Zealand brands or via intermediaries, including 
insurance brokers and bank partners. We generally have annual contracts with customers and premiums are calculated at each renewal 
based on a range of factors including individual risk factors and changing input costs such as reinsurance and claims inflation.
Our strategy is to grow our business through creating connected customer experiences across our brands. We intend to continue to 
digitalise the business, enhance our data and AI capabilities, and create more personalised customer experiences. Our strategy is in 
service of our purpose: we make your world a safer place.

1.3	 IAG New Zealand entity level scenarios
IAG New Zealand was involved in creating the Insurance Council of New Zealand | Te Kāhui Inihua o Aotearoa insurance sector climate 
scenarios (ICNZ scenarios) in FY22 and those scenarios continue to be used as a basis for our own entity-level scenarios.5 For FY25, IAG 
New Zealand reviewed and refreshed our climate scenarios for relevance and plausibility so they appropriately test the resilience of 
our business. Changes included reflecting current government adaptation policies and increased inequality assumptions over time. 
The scenario refresh builds on our FY24 scenario analysis which leveraged the physical risk models underpinning our insurance and 
reinsurance risk assessments, with overlays applied to reflect the projected physical risk changes across a range of natural peril types. 
The refresh was informed by IAG New Zealand’s transition planning process, alongside engagement with IAG Group on the development 
of Group-wide scenario narratives, as well as by retesting the scenarios with the Climate Working Group6. In FY25, the timeframe 
associated with the short-term scenario was rolled forward to start one year later. These changes were approved by the Climate 
Disclosure Steering Committee. Our climate scenario analysis was undertaken as part of IAG New Zealand’s transition planning and 
wider strategy processes.7

1.4	 Current physical and transition impacts of climate change on our business
We have identified one current material climate-related impact on IAG New Zealand, being the physical impact of large (or ‘recognised’) 
weather-related events.11 Recognised weather-related events can materially impact claims costs, reinsurance expenses, and 
underwriting profitability. We set out below the current financial impacts to IAG New Zealand of recognised weather-related events.  
All numbers are rounded to the nearest million dollars. 
There were 32 recognised weather-related events during FY25.
The total gross claims cost from recognised weather-related events in FY25 was $132 million, which was partially offset by $26 million 
positive claims reserve releases from prior periods, resulting in a net impact before reinsurance of $106 million. Reinsurance recoveries 
of $34 million resulted in a net claims cost of $72 million recognised in FY25. 
The gross outstanding claims liability12 for weather-related events as at 30 June 2025 for IAG New Zealand was $222 million (a decrease 
of $84 million from 30 June 2024). This amount includes outstanding claims for weather-related events in prior financial years. 
During FY25 claims payments for weather-related claims resulted in cash outflows of $204 million. This amount includes payments in 
respect of claims for weather-related events in prior financial years.
Aotearoa New Zealand experienced less severe recognised weather-related events in FY25 and FY24 when compared with FY23 (which 
included the North Island floods and Cyclone Gabrielle). 
IAG New Zealand has not identified any material current transition impacts for FY25. Current transition impacts observed but which 
are not material include impacts driven by regulatory requirements, customer preferences, and the shift towards a low-carbon 
economy. These impacts have influenced capital deployment decisions including pursuing efficiency initiatives and compliance-related 
expenditure.

1.7	 Transition planning process
IAG New Zealand engaged with stakeholders from across the business, with support from consultants WSP, to develop its transition 
planning framework. We used scenario analysis and assessment of climate-related risks and opportunities to identify key themes, 
longer-term desired outcomes and short-term actions that have been incorporated into our three-year business plan. These address 
material and non-material climate-related risks and opportunities.
1.7.1	 Capital deployment
Management of climate-related risks and opportunities forms part of our decision-making processes for capital deployment and funding 
including through internal budgeting processes. Our transition planning includes initiatives that require capital allocation, which are 
considered as part of our annual business planning cycle. Capital expenditure towards climate-related risks and opportunities is set out 
in the capital deployment metric in Table 4. For a breakdown of capital deployment initiatives in FY25, see the Notes section.
In addition, there are existing processes involving capital deployment relating to:
•	 our capital and reinsurance strategy; 
•	 the setting and allocation of the Natural Perils Allowance;16 
•	 assessment of reinsurance costs; and
•	 government advocacy around our climate response. 
Both IAG New Zealand and Group continue to invest in data capability to improve our management of climate-related and other peril 
risk across our insurance portfolio. This year, we have continued to update our flooding and coastal inundation hazard mapping, 
incorporating lessons from recent weather events in our other peril models and addressing known modelling limitations. From a 
government advocacy perspective, we continue to allocate resource and funding to research around climate impacts, which supports 
our advocacy efforts.
